newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to free drugs prices next year - report.
newsitem.headline: Poland to free drugs prices next year - report.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to free prices of drugs as of next year, which may lift them by about 40 percent but it is necessary to complete the pharmaceutical sector's privatisation, a newspaper reported.

On Wednesday Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted deputy health minister Wojciech Kusmierkiewicz as saying that the government is likely to decide in June on freeing prices of some 30 percent of drugs which remain officially controlled.
"We may consider freeing drug prices in two stages so as not to hit people's pockets," Kusmierkiewicz was quoted as saying.
Polish drug makers say the liberalisation is necessary to complete the privatisation of the pharmaceutical sector, which has so far involved only two companies -- Polfa Kutno and Jelfa.

The government plans to sell five more companies from the sector this year, with public tenders for Polfa Rzeszow and Polfa Krakow already opened and tenders for Polfa Poznan, Polfa Starogard and Polfa Tarchomin planned later this year.
Zycie Warszawy daily quoted deputy treasury minister Andrzej Peczak as confirming earlier reports that Polfa Kutno and Jelfa were bidding for Rzeszow and Krakow.
